chunks: Abu Qurra the narrator asked me to take him to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him). So I sought his permission, and he permitted me. He entered and asked him about the permissible and the forbidden, then said to him: 'Do you acknowledge that God is carried?'

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Every carried thing is acted upon, attributed to something other than itself, and in need. The word "carried" is a term of deficiency in expression, while "carrier" is an agent and is praiseworthy in expression. Similarly are the words of one who says "above" and "below" and "higher" and "lower". God has said: "And to God belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them" [7:180] — and He did not say in His books that He is the carried one; rather He said that He is the Carrier on land and sea, and the Upholder of the heavens and the earth lest they decline. The "carried" is that which is other than God, and never has anyone who believes in God and His Majesty been heard to say in their supplication: "O Carried One!"'

Abu Qurra said: 'But He said: "And above them eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord on that Day" [69:17], and He said: "Those who bear the Throne" [40:7].' Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'The Throne is not God. The Throne is a name of knowledge and power — a throne in which everything exists. Then He attributed the carrying to others of His creation, because He subjugated His creation through the carrying of His Throne — and they carry His knowledge. And He created beings who glorify around His Throne, performing by His knowledge, and angels who record the deeds of His servants; and He subjugated the people of the earth through circumambulation around His House. And God settled upon the Throne as He said.'

The Throne, and those who carry it, and those around the Throne — God is their Carrier, their Preserver, the Upholder, the Standing One over every soul, above everything, and upon everything. He cannot be called "the carried" nor "the lower" as a standalone word without connection to something else, for that would corrupt the word and the meaning.

Abu Qurra said: 'Are you denying the report which states that when God is angry, His anger is known because the angels who carry the Throne feel its weight upon their shoulders and fall prostrate? And when the anger subsides, it becomes lighter and they return to their places.'

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Tell me about God, Blessed and Exalted — since He cursed Iblis until this day of yours, He has been angry with him; so when did He become pleased? And according to your description, He does not cease to be angry with him, with his followers, and with his supporters. How do you dare to describe your Lord with change from one state to another, and that what flows upon creatures flows upon Him? Glorified is He and Exalted — He does not decline along with those who decline, nor does He change with those who change, nor alter with those who alter. Those below Him are in His hand and His management; all of them are in need of Him, and He is needless of any besides Him.'

key_terms.الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى: The Most Beautiful Names — Quranic concept that God's names are attributes of praise; 'carried' is not among them
key_terms.الْحَامِلُ: The Carrier — the active agent; the Imam affirms God is the Carrier (sustainer) of all things
key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: The Throne — interpreted by the Imam as a name representing divine knowledge and power, not a literal physical throne
key_terms.الْمُمْسِكُ: The Upholder/Sustainer — one of God's active attributes, contrasted with the passive 'carried'
key_terms.تَنْزِيهٌ: Divine transcendence — the principle that God cannot be described with creaturely attributes
key_terms.سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى: Glorified and Exalted — a formula of divine transcendence used to conclude the Imam's argument
key_terms.مَحْمُولٌ: Carried — a passive participle implying being acted upon by another, which the Imam argues is impossible for God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about whether God can be described as 'carried' (محمول)?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS) engages in a theological debate with Abu Qurra, a Sunni hadith scholar, who asks whether God can be described as 'carried' (محمول). The Imam refutes this anthropomorphic concept through precise linguistic and rational analysis: the word 'carried' implies passivity, need, and dependence — attributes impossible for God. He explains that the Quranic references to the Throne being carried refer to the Throne as a locus of knowledge and power, not to God Himself. The Imam further dismantles the idea of God's anger causing physical heaviness to the angels carrying the Throne, demonstrating that attributing changing emotional states to God — like creatures — contradicts divine transcendence (tanzih). This dialogue reflects the theological milieu of Imam al-Rida's era (early 3rd century AH) when Mutazilite, Murji'ite, and various hadith-based traditions debated divine attributes vigorously at the Abbasid court.
